page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ise.xlarge is a member of the Enhanced instance family configured on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the system supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Compute resources are paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an even distribution of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance contains no integrated graphics processing units, dedicating all host resources strictly to conventional central processing.

Storage and networking capabilities reflect a decoupled cloud infrastructure model. The server contains no local storage, requiring all operating system files and persistent data volumes to be hosted on network-attached block storage. Network interfaces provide a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps for communication within virtual networks. Additionally, the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring elastic IP allocation or gateway routing for external network reachability.

With its standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.g8ise.xlarge delivers cost-efficient resource density for applications that do not require local NVMe caching or specialized accelerators. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing execution without resource contention from burstable shares. This configuration fits standard enterprise workloads, including web application serving, containerized services, microservices backbones, and continuous integration build nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ise.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family, designed around a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Powered by the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, the server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8475B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core). The instance does not bundle local storage or GPU hardware, requiring external network-attached block storage for operating system and application data persistence. Network connectivity provides a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default. By focusing entirely on dedicated CPU and memory without the cost overhead of local disks or acceleration silicon, the server offers efficient resource allocation for mid-tier web serving, microservices, containerized deployments, and standard enterprise applications.
